description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10), probed vs perl 5.40.3.

`reset` is a NO-OP STUB.  `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`'s `p-reset` ignores its
argument and returns 1, with the docstring "Perl reset - reset ?? searches.
No-op in PCL".  Perl's `reset EXPR` does TWO things, and only the second is
covered by a not-supported entry:

  (a) it CLEARS every package variable in the current package whose name begins
      with one of the listed letters -- scalars to undef, arrays and hashes to
      empty;
  (b) it re-arms every `?pattern?` one-match search in the current package.

REPRODUCER (perl | PCL):
    package Foo;
    $aa = "abc"; @ab = (1,2,3); %ac = (k => 'v');
    reset 'a';
    print defined $Foo::aa ? $Foo::aa : "UNDEF";   # perl UNDEF | PCL abc
    print scalar @Foo::ab;                          # perl 0     | PCL 3
    print scalar keys %Foo::ac;                     # perl 0     | PCL 1

Half (b) is already `docs/not-supported.md` "`reset()` for one-match `?pattern?`
and named captures".  Half (a) is NOT written down anywhere, and it is the one
that silently does nothing.

ROWS: t/op/reset.t is 19 blessed fail rows and every one of them is this --
"reset 'char'", "reset 'chars'", "reset 'range'", "reset \"\\0char\"",
"resetting an array", "resetting a hash", "match doesn't match second time"
(the `?pattern?` half) and the read-only/glob guards around them.

SIZE: half (a) is a bounded runtime job -- walk the current package's symbol
table, match the leading character against the letter/range spec (perl's spec
is a character class without the brackets: `reset "a-z"`), and clear the SCALAR,
ARRAY and HASH slots, skipping read-only ones (perl croaks
"Modification of a read-only value attempted" for those, which two rows assert).
It needs `%p-current-package`'s stash, which the glob work (#1664) also wants;
do the two together or make sure this one does not grow a second stash walker.
Rule 12 applies to the stub as it stands: it returns 1 and writes nothing.
subject: `reset EXPR` is a no-op stub: perl CLEARS every package variable whose name starts with a listed letter, PCL leaves them (op/reset.t, all 19 rows)
